title: Weekly journal, a new editor, MFE/MAE in ticks and trades step by step
body: The biggest update so far: plan, run and review your trading week in one place, write everything in one new editor and see how much of each move you actually took.

new: Weekly journal: plan the week, follow it day by day and close it with a review. News and holidays show next to each day, and the next week opens as soon as you close one.
Log a trade step by step right from the Week: plan, entry, close. The full trade form is split into the same three parts.
One new editor everywhere - Notes, market notes, day plan, trade notes, Playbook and the Week. Multi-level lists, collapsible sections, wrapped images, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y.
Exit type: tag how you left a trade (Planned target, BE, Partial + runner BE, Full SL, Trailing SL). Edit the list in Playbook; statistics and bulk edit use it too.

MFE and MAE are on by default and entered in ticks (pips for forex) - the number TradingView's Measure tool shows. R is still calculated from your stop, so statistics stay comparable across instruments.

Exit efficiency right in the trade form: furthest exit : MFE × 100, with every step of the calculation shown. The furthest exit is taken from your best exit price (or R × stop, or money) - press Calculate or type it yourself.
Edit your Confluences, Mistakes, Emotions and Exit types in a popup straight from the trade form - no need to leave the trade.
Updates written during a trade can be edited.
Pick more than one mood in a journal entry, and edit your own mood list right where you choose it.
System rules are written directly in Playbook.
TradingView import now brings commissions, stop loss and take profit from protective orders, and accepts up to five files at once.
Import orders from a chart screenshot: the AI reads lines like "2 @ 21450" into an editable table before anything is saved.
AI settings: choose a provider and load its model list with one click. Errors from the provider are explained in plain words.
Support chat with the developer and a Community chat with other traders (anonymous by default) - in the web app.
Account tab in Settings: profile with nickname and country flag, password, passkeys and account deletion.
A "Notifications not arriving?" guide inside the app.
fixed: Week P&L is now after fees (commissions, fees and slippage), for the week total and each trade in it.
Deleting an account that had a passkey, push notifications or an MT5 token failed.
Ctrl+V pastes the image where your mouse is - even while the cursor sits in the trade note, and never into two places at once.
Pasting an image no longer opens the file picker.
Sticky columns no longer slide under the top bar.
Hidden buttons in the notifications settings stayed visible.
"Rules and guardrails" and "Questions and outside influences" in the Week no longer collapse after every click.
changed: Reflection and the weekly review save themselves as you type.
The image viewer moves between images with the arrow keys only, and zoom is at least 2x centered on the point you clicked.
Password reset e-mail is a proper HTML mail, and its link is valid for 30 minutes. New accounts get a welcome e-mail and the tutorial follows today's app.
Habits fill the width of the panel and their checkboxes keep a fixed width.

title: Backtests, links in notes, subtasks and market notes in sync
body: Market notes now sync between the desktop app and the cloud, photos included.

new: Backtests: log a practice trade exactly like a live one, just switch the mode next to the title. It never touches your live statistics.
A backtest run is a named period. A trade joins it by its entry time, and the run shows net R, win rate, profit factor and an equity curve.
Links inside notes: type // to link another page, a trade or a model. The target page shows how many notes link to it.
Market-note images can be captioned, including in the zoomed view.
Subtasks: every quick task can have its own checklist. Checking the task off checks all its subtasks.
Market notes (with their photos and captions) sync between the desktop app and the web. Deleting one moves it to the bin on the other side too.
fixed: Editing a journal entry from the Dashboard feed opened an empty form after a page refresh - and saving it overwrote the entry with blanks.
A backtest trade that fell into no run was unreachable from the interface. It now has its own row.
The block handle in Notes drifted up and down while scrolling.
changed: Photos in market notes keep their original quality instead of always being re-encoded and shrunk.
Their thumbnails show the whole chart instead of cropping it, and the caption sits under the photo like it does for trades.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.3
body: Since 1.9.1 the app updates itself — look for the update banner in the sidebar, installing takes a couple of clicks. The 1.9.x series added auto-updates, more reliable background shutdown, and English as the default language for fresh installs.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.4 — please reinstall manually
body: 1.9.4 is out, but auto-update can't deliver it to your install: the signing key had to be replaced after the original password was permanently lost, and every copy up to 1.9.3 only trusts the old key. This is a one-time thing — download and run the 1.9.4 installer from the releases page (github.com/JZ-laboratory/journal-releases/releases), your trades and journal are untouched by the reinstall. After that, auto-update works normally again with the new key. 1.9.4 also adds a Cloud Sync section in Settings if you want to link an account at trading-diary.co, and wider Dashboard layouts on large monitors.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.5
body: 1.9.5 brings two-way cloud sync: trades, accounts, models, journal entries, Notebook notes and reflections now sync automatically between the desktop app and your linked account at trading-diary.co, in both directions — link your account once in Settings → Cloud Sync and it runs on its own from then on (a "Sync now" button is there too if you want it instant). Your look and feel — accent color, background animation, language — follows you between devices too. Anything that can't sync safely, like two conflicting edits, shows up as a clear entry in the Cloud Sync panel instead of silently picking a winner.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.6
body: 1.9.6 makes the sync rules clearer and safer. Your cloud account is now the reference copy: when you're online, the desktop app catches up to it automatically, and the only thing that ever holds a record back is an edit you made here that hasn't reached the cloud yet — a genuine conflict (the same record changed in two places) still always shows up for you to resolve, never silently overwritten either way. Also fixed: deleting something for good now waits until that deletion has actually reached the cloud first, so an old cloud copy can never quietly bring it back.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.7
body: 1.9.7 makes sync feel instant. When the app pulls in something new from the cloud — a trade someone added elsewhere, a setting you changed on another device — it quietly refreshes itself in the background. No more reloading to see it show up. Appearance sync now also covers font, blur, transparency and light/dark theme, on top of accent color, background and language from 1.9.5.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.8
body: 1.9.8 finishes the sync story: trade screenshots now sync between desktop and your cloud account too, the last piece after trades, accounts, journal, and Notebook in earlier 1.9.x releases. Your account email and log out are now always visible in the sidebar instead of tucked into the top bar, with a confirmation before you actually log out. The top bar also has a manual reopen arrow now if you scroll it out of view. Send feedback is more reliable too — it wasn't always reaching us before. And a round of polish: hover states and tooltips are more consistent across the app, and the New Trade form and the news/quotes strip both make better use of extra width on large monitors.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.9
body: A small fix release: the top bar's manual reopen arrow now sits correctly across every screen layout and window width, instead of occasionally landing in the wrong spot.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.10 — accounts are now required
body: Starting with 1.9.10, the desktop app requires a linked account from first launch — it's how your data stays safe and available across devices now, not an optional toggle anymore. If you don't have one yet, you'll need an invite code to register. Already have an account? Nothing changes, you just log straight in. Beyond that: Focus Strip quotes and your Goals & Discipline targets now sync across devices too. The Focus Strip itself got several layout fixes — no more empty gaps when it has little to show, and its placeholder text is properly centered. The app also quietly checks for updates in the background every couple of hours now, not just on launch.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.11
body: A small maintenance release with no visible changes — internal groundwork ahead of the next few updates.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.12
body: 1.9.12 fixes a cloud sync gap: quotes, Notebook folders, tags and images that already existed when you first linked your account weren't always being picked up on your other devices — pull now correctly recognizes them, and anything missed will catch up automatically on the next sync. A settings value that can't be traced back to either side now shows up for you to review in Settings instead of being handled silently, same as other sync conflicts. Also added a missing translation for one conflict message that was showing raw text instead of a readable sentence.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.13
body: 1.9.13 adds a dedicated Reflections page — a queue of trades still waiting for their post-trade reflection up top, and a full overview below with status filters, replacing the old popup. Trades gained a Reflection status column, and a new "Table columns" button lets you hide the ones you don't need (Date, Instrument and Side always stay visible) — your choice syncs across devices. You can now move a batch of selected trades to a different account in one go, and all three trash bins (Trades, Accounts, Notebook) support selecting several items at once to restore or permanently delete. Notebook pages can be bulk-edited too — move to a section, add or remove tags, change status or priority, or delete several at once. Also fixed: the Focus Strip ticker now scrolls at a genuinely constant speed no matter how wide your window is (it used to blur together on large monitors), plus a handful of smaller cloud sync reliability fixes.

title: Trading Diary 1.9.15
body: Fixes an issue where the sidebar could get stuck collapsed after scrolling. Also fixes two-factor authentication setup (regenerating your QR code no longer silently invalidates your existing authenticator entry) and makes the QR code on the Account page reliably scannable. Sign-in and cloud account screens got clearer error messages and a small visual refresh.

title: Trading Diary 2.0.0
body: 2.0.0 is the biggest update yet. A trade chart (Settings → Beta features) shows a real candlestick chart for any trade, with entry/exit arrows and SL/TP lines drawn right on it — powered by live market data, no manual setup needed. Voice input lets you dictate a brand-new trade in one go, or fill in any single form field by speaking instead of typing — it works fully offline, with an AI fallback only if the offline parser can't make sense of what you said. If you link a MetaTrader 5 account at trading-diary.co, an EA can now auto-import your trades into the cloud in the background — no manual export/import round-trip. Smaller additions: trade screenshots can now be browsed as a full gallery in the lightbox instead of one at a time, and background animations plus the top bar got a real performance and visual pass (less stutter, sharper rendering).

title: Trading Diary 2.1.0
body:
2.1.0 adds a market log to the Journal: a record of the market itself, not just of your trades. An entry is a timestamped observation — instrument, a chart, what you expect, and, filled in later, what actually happened. That gap is the point: you write the expectation now and the outcome when it plays out, even days later. Days without a trade stop being holes in your history — you pick why you didn’t trade, or what the market was doing (range, trending, volatile, thin).

Above it sits a feed: one timeline of market notes, trades, journal entries and economic news, with your own choice of what appears and how far back. Images swipe sideways, everything is searchable, and on a wide screen the feed becomes a column on the right with its own scrollbar. News now reach back as far as the range promises, because the app keeps its own archive instead of asking the provider for the current week only. The same feed is available as a Dashboard tile.

The two journal fields are now called “What I’m bringing into the day” and “How the day went” — they were never only about the market, and the old names said otherwise. Editing a journal entry or a market note always happens in one window, opened from anywhere, and it finally lets you fix the date of an entry that landed on the wrong day. Deleting is split, so removing the morning half leaves the evening one alone, and anything you delete waits 30 days in a bin you can restore from.
